expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/, the kind the map gives a foundation decision such as the job queue.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: Context opens with the incident: "On Saturday night Redis ran out of memory and evicted keys, including queued receipt jobs, without logging an error... About 300 members were affected; resending their receipts by hand from the orders table took most of a volunteer's Tuesday." It then adds "Redis served only the job queue, and only one operations volunteer knew how to restore it" and names the forces ("protect queued work, keep an order and its job from being separated by a failure, and reduce the services volunteers had to operate"). The choice of procrastinate comes only in Options and Decision.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md': '## Decision\n\nBackground jobs live in Postgres, using procrastinate, and Redis is no longer needed for the queue. Procras'}
